purpose: VibeVoice-ASR Q4_K_M end-to-end real-time factor and stage attribution on real speech
hardware: AMD Ryzen AI MAX+ PRO 395, Radeon 8060S (gfx1151), 256-bit LPDDR5X, 133 GB unified

protocol.weights: Q4_K_M GGUF backbone (raw blocks, no repack), bf16 front-end encoders + connectors
protocol.workload: LibriSpeech test-clean utterances at 24 kHz mono, round-robin across speakers; greedy decode, max_new_tokens 256, seed 20260914
protocol.matched_request: each clip's request is regenerated through the bench's prepare lane (HF processor, frozen seed) so both lanes consume identical PCM, noise, scales and prompt ids
protocol.timing_boundaries: each stage is bracketed by device synchronizes, so a stage is execution wall time rather than enqueue time. Weight loading, tokenization, request preparation and WER scoring are outside every timer. Real-time factor is total wall time / audio duration; the pooled value is total time over total audio (duration-weighted), the median is the median of per-clip RTFs.

prior_200clip_rows.note: recorded on the same host before the decode-scratch, prefill-arena and Q6_K down-projection changes landed; kept for context, not as a like-for-like comparison since the clip sets and durations differ

gates.wer: 1.37% on the 40-clip run (Whisper-normalized jiwer micro-average over parsed Content), consistent with the 2.011% recorded over 200 clips
gates.correctness: same production path as the WER gate: 16 passed / 1 xfailed in tests/test_gpu_vibevoice_qwen2_q4_runner.py
gates.consistency: the two independent runs agree: pooled RTF 0.354 with no stage timers over 40 clips, 0.360 with per-stage synchronizes over 20 clips

profile.why: this is a timing measurement of the existing production path; it changes no arithmetic.
profile.not_claimed: real-time factor is not a production qualification. WER is the task-quality gate here and it passes, but the calibrated KL envelope, isolation and BF16-relative gates are recorded elsewhere.

notes: Decode dominates: 81.3% of end-to-end time, against 9.9% batched prefill and 8.8% front-end. Prompt assembly is 0.0% (37 ms over 20 clips).
Decode is a bandwidth-bound GEMV: 5.012 GB of Q4_K_M weights streamed per token against 14.15 GB for the dense bf16 lane, which is where the 1.55x decode ratio comes from.

RTF is dominated by the token-to-audio ratio, not by audio length alone. The 20-clip stage run pools to 0.360 but its per-clip median is 0.239, because most clips reach EOS in about 30 tokens while one 22.6 s clip hit the 256-token cap at RTF 0.625. Both numbers are reported for that reason.
Excluding decode, the rest of the pipeline is about 19% of end-to-end time, so further RTF work is decode work.

The 40-clip run's mean is 3.287 s/clip against the 3.477 s/clip recorded on the 200-clip run before today's scratch changes; the clip sets differ, so this is context rather than a measured same-suite delta.
